messages:
sam: Heads-up — seeing a burst of AER/corrected PCIe errors across a couple of GPU-heavy nodes in us-west-2. Batch job tail latency and eviction rate spiked ~20% around 03:10 UTC. Ops bot posted alerts.
ops-bot: [alert] cluster-gpu-3: node-23/node-24 AER rate > baseline (5m rolling) :rotating_light:
anya: Can you paste the dmesg / Xid snippets? Xid codes will tell us whether it's hardware vs driver.
sam: Paste from node-24 kern log around spike:
```
[Mar 18 03:09:54] pcie 0000:03:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=12
[Mar 18 03:09:54] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 57, pid=12345, VN=thread-7
[Mar 18 03:09:55] nvme0n1: reset controller
[Mar 18 03:09:56] gpu0: ECC counters: device 3, corrected 139 -> 162
```
kevin: Xid 57 usually points to microcode/firmware or transient memory errors. ECC bump also suggests hardware path. Did we push any BIOS/kernel updates recently?
jordan: We did a quiet BIOS microcode push to rack12 last week to address thermal reporting. No kernel updates since. @kevin could that correlate?
zara: Regional note: us-west-2 is running higher A100 reserved workloads today — can't drain too many nodes without impacting SLOs. We should prefer non-prod time or stagger.
anya: Proposal: isolate node-24 first (most noisy), run mem/cpu/GPU stress with monitoring, swap the PCIe riser on node-24 if repro, and test a warm reboot vs full power cycle. If errors persist, tag the GPU for RMA. Thoughts?
sam: Agreed. I can run a short reproducer: 10min transformer microbench + cuda_memtest on node-24. Will stream logs here. If Xid persists under load, we RMA.
kevin: Also check NVLink counters. Even if AERs are on PCIe path, NVLink errors can cascade into GPU Xids under heavy traffic.
anya: Quick command to pull counters:
```
nvlinkstats -i 0 --show-errors
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,REPLAY
dmesg | grep -i xid
```
sam: Ran nvlinkstats on node-24 — reported sporadic link retransmits on NVLink-1 during peak. Not huge but correlated with AER bursts. nvlink logs:
```
NVLink: link 1 retransmit count +18 in 60s
NVLink: ecc parity corrected +2
```
zara: Could be hot neighbor effect — rack power rail or riser contact. Rack12 PSU shows stable readings though.
jordan: Ops: can we schedule a 30m staggered drain for node-24 at 21:30 PT? We'll keep one of the reserved A100 pools for failover to avoid customer impact.
zara: 21:30 PT works. I'll open a maintenance window and notify support.
ops-bot: [action] drain job started: ./infra/drain_node.sh node-24 --evict --timeout 1200
sam: Running repro now (starting 03:38 UTC): transformer microbench + cuda_memtest. Streaming failures: got Xid 31 after 5m, then Xid 57 repeat after warm reboot.
anya: Xid 31 then 57 sequence — sounds like memory path error followed by uncaught device fault. Suspect flaky riser or card.
kevin: If reboot didn't clear it, try reseating the GPU and swapping riser slots. If problem moves with card -> RMA card. If stays on slot -> riser/mobo issue.
jordan: Who can do physical reseat in us-west-2 data center? Ops team: @oncall-infra?
sam: @oncall-infra I can be onsite, will reseat GPU and test in 2h post maintenance. Will also run a reduced load test to validate.
zara: Reminder: create a temporary routing rule to avoid scheduling long nightly batch jobs on rack12 until we confirm fix.
kevin: Also create a short-term autoscale to shift batch capacity to us-east-1 to smooth SLOs tonight.
anya: Action items:
- sam: reseat card, run repro, report results (if fails -> tag GPU for RMA)
- jordan: schedule maintenance, open support incident with RMA priority
- zara: apply scheduling constraints + autoscale shift
- kevin: follow up on BIOS microcode fingerprinting

sam: After reseat and swap (21:55 PT) — errors stopped under the same synthetic load for 20m. No Xids observed. Node returned to service.
jordan: Great. We'll keep it under observation for 24h. If errors recur, we escalate RMA and hardware replacement.
zara: Logging the case: INV-2026-1834, note intermittent AER -> NVLink retransmit cascade, likely riser contact. Cost note: RMA for a single A100 + shipping ~ $2k, but replacing a riser is ~$400 and same-day swap might be faster.
kevin: Marking hypothesis: riser contact + heavy NVLink traffic causing ECC increment -> Xid cascade. Follow-up: check firmware rollback window on affected nodes and consider targeted microcode revert if pattern reappears.
ops-bot: [monitoring] node-23/node-24 AER rate back to baseline. Closing high-severity alert.
anya: Nice triage. We'll annotate the incident with logs and the reproduction steps so on-call can run same checks next time. :white_check_mark:
